title: Flooding and Climate Change in East Africa
excerpt: Deadly floods across Kenya, Tanzania and Burundi show how climate change and poor planning fall hardest on women and girls.
body:
Floods swept across Kenya, Tanzania and Burundi in 2024, costing hundreds of lives, displacing thousands of families and destroying farmland, roads and homes.

## Who carries the burden

In Kenya, women and girls bear a disproportionate share of the loss: caring for displaced families, rebuilding livelihoods and facing greater risk in temporary shelters.

## Climate and infrastructure

The scale of the damage reflects both a changing climate and failures of planning: building in flood-prone areas and inadequate drainage.

> We need to focus on resilience and empowerment.

## A call for support

WOPCAA calls for flood-resilient planning that puts the women who hold communities together at the centre of recovery.
author: Skitter Mbugua, PhD

title: Voices of Resilience: Maasai Women COP Mashinani
excerpt: Our abstract on the resilience of Maasai women was selected for a symposium on operationalising a just transition in Africa.
body:
WOPCAA's abstract on the resilience of Maasai women was selected for a symposium and publication on operationalising a just transition in Africa, supported by IDRC with the University of Pretoria's Environmental Humanities Programme, the African Research Impact Network and SouthSouthNorth.

The abstract draws on COP Mashinani and on the experience of women living with the impacts of climate change in Kajiado. Our team returned to Isinya to record their stories in their own words.

Thank you to the community for welcoming us. More updates will follow.
author: WOPCAA

title: Advancing Climate Resilience and Sustainable Peace: Empowering Women as Agents of Change
excerpt: Climate change is a threat multiplier, and women are both the most exposed and the pillars of peace in their communities.
body:
## Climate change as a threat multiplier

Climate change strains agriculture, water, health and access to resources, and deepens existing inequalities. Women, with less decision-making power, are the most exposed.

## Women as pillars of peacebuilding

Women mediate, lead grassroots resilience, steward the environment and build bridges across communities and borders.

## What it takes

- Climate literacy, skills and economic empowerment
- Gender-inclusive climate finance
- Legal protections and intersectional policy
- Global partnerships, knowledge exchange and inclusive decision-making

## A call to action

WOPCAA invites like-minded organisations to partner with us in putting women at the centre of climate resilience and sustainable peace.
author: Skitter Mbugua, PhD

title: Empowering Women for Climate Resilience: Unraveling the Interconnected Web of Climate Change and Health
excerpt: How climate change and health interact, and why the effects fall hardest on vulnerable women.
body: Heat, floods, drought and food insecurity are health crises as much as climate ones. This article looks at how climate change and health interact, and at why the effects fall hardest on vulnerable women.
author: Skitter Mbugua, PhD

title: Strategic Planning for a Sustainable Future
excerpt: WOPCAA began developing a strategic plan as a roadmap for women's climate resilience in Kajiado and beyond.
body:
At the Kenya Electoral Conflict Mitigation and Civic Voter Education Support (ECCES) programme, our Executive Director, Dr. Skitter Wangeci Mbugua, led discussions on developing WOPCAA's strategic plan: a roadmap for women's climate resilience.

The plan answers the call for more environmental conservation work, with one aim: a resilient, just future for women in Kajiado and beyond.

title: Climate Resilience and Sustainable Agriculture
excerpt: Sustainable farming protects food security while cutting agriculture's carbon footprint.
body:
Climate change challenges agriculture everywhere. Sustainable farming supports food security and lowers the sector's carbon footprint.

Practices such as no-till farming, crop rotation and agroforestry improve soil health, conserve water and cut emissions. They support biodiversity and reduce reliance on synthetic pesticides and fertilisers.

Healthy soils also store carbon, helping communities both adapt to and mitigate climate change.
author: WOPCAA

title: The Role of Women in Climate Action
excerpt: Women are agents of change in climate action, across communities, economies and policy.
body:
Women are agents of change in climate action, across communities, economies and policy.

They lead on climate resilience, sustainable agriculture, reforestation and resource management, and shape climate-resilient policy and green technology.

Including women in decisions is key to handling climate-related conflict and building resilient societies.
